headline: Medical examiner rules Woodbridge couple’s deaths a homicide-suicide
dek: Jo Ann and William Karales were found after an employee requested a welfare check at their Orchard Road home; police said the incident was isolated and posed no known danger to the public.
body: The deaths of a Woodbridge couple found inside their Orchard Road home have been ruled a homicide-suicide, according to findings from Connecticut’s Office of the Chief Medical Examiner and statements from local police.

Jo Ann Karales, 66, died from a shotgun wound to the neck and her manner of death was classified as homicide, the medical examiner’s office told news organizations. William Karales, 71, died from a gunshot wound to the head and his manner of death was classified as suicide. NBC Connecticut reported the findings after the couple’s bodies were taken to the medical examiner’s office in Farmington.

The couple was found Friday, Oct. 2, after an employee of their business told police the homeowners had not shown up for work and could not be reached. Woodbridge police were called to the home at about 11:49 a.m. for a well-being check, according to the department’s account reported by NBC Connecticut and [CT Insider](https://www.ctinsider.com/connecticut/article/woodbridge-joann-william-karales-murder-suicide-22462568.php).

Officers entered through a rear window and found both people dead inside, police said. The Connecticut State Police Western District Major Crime Squad assisted Woodbridge investigators with processing the scene. Police initially described the matter as an isolated incident and said there was no known danger to the surrounding community.

The medical examiner’s findings answered how the two people died but did not publicly establish what led to the shooting. Police had initially declined to characterize the deaths while the examination and investigation were pending. As of Monday, authorities had not disclosed a motive or described any other person as a suspect. The distinction matters: the medical examiner’s ruling classifies the manners of death, while the investigative record may still be incomplete.

The deaths also affect a small Connecticut company with a local employment connection. CT Insider reported that William and Jo Ann Karales operated Sea Lark Enterprises, the Woodbridge-based business behind Soap Lift, a product designed to keep bar soap raised so water can drain away. The report said the business grew from an operation William Karales started in his Long Island garage and eventually shipped products beyond Connecticut.

CT Insider also reported that the company worked with the Amity Transition Academy, a program serving students with intellectual disabilities, to provide paid packaging work. That background gives the case a community dimension beyond the Orchard Road investigation: the couple’s deaths leave questions for relatives, employees and people who knew the business through that employment partnership.

Woodbridge police extended condolences to the Karales family and thanked the state police major-crimes investigators who assisted. The department’s public statements, as reported by NBC Connecticut, did not announce additional arrests or charges. Further information would have to come from investigators or the medical examiner as the case record develops.
